column7: resolveID and fetchValue required nothing of a matching list entry or value response beyond the name/id already asked for, so a server-side filter or lookup bug could return a same-named secret from a different project or environment and the agent would materialise it under the intended name (follow-up review after #4568). Both now require the returned project_id, environment_id (and for fetchValue, id) to equal what was requested, else a plain error -- deliberately not ErrUpstreamGone, so the engine marks the target failed and retries rather than treating the mismatch as proof the secret was removed and wiping the synced copy. TestFetcher_ValueOutsideScopeFailsClosed covers the value-side half of this fix (not this row's proving test); TestFetcher_InScopeResponseStillDelivers is the liveness control pinning that correctly-scoped responses still deliver. Not covered: a fully attacker-controlled server that stamps the expected scope on a fabricated response (INV-KSYNC-fetch-scope-fail-closed says so).
